day_shape: 87 items: US Treasury moves to sever Banque Misr UAE and Bank Melli Dubai from dollar system under "Operation Economic Outcast", CENTCOM says Hormuz mines cleared, IDF strikes kill Hamas Jenin commander Qais Bitawi and Gaza operatives, heavy Khamenei Government Week message cycle.

threads.label: US "Economic Outcast" sanctions push
threads.summary: The State Department and Treasury announced sanctions on Bank Melli's Dubai branch manager Reza Mohammad Taeedi and moved to revoke Banque Misr UAE's US correspondent banking access, calling it a "critical node" for Iranian dollar flows. Iran International framed the Banque Misr action as the first major strike of Washington's "Economic D-Day", while WSJ reported Iranian banks continue operating in Dubai.

threads.label: Tehran responses to economic pressure
threads.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry called the US campaign "state terrorism" and Defa Press cited a Reuters framing of a "costly stalemate"; SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatened US economic interests if the maritime blockade continues but also set out four conditions for a deal. Defence Ministry spokesman Talai-Nik and the Acting Defence Minister said "surprises" await enemies.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and mediation track
threads.summary: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said the US military has cleared Iranian sea mines from Hormuz shipping lanes, echoed by Trump, while Iran International reported Gulf states pouring billions into routes bypassing the strait. Three regional mediators visited Tehran in three days seeking to revive US-Iran talks, with Trump reportedly moving away from June's MoU terms.

threads.label: Khamenei Government Week message
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRIB published a long Government Week message praising the Pezeshkian cabinet's actions under "intensified sanctions and blockades", declaring anything harming social cohesion "forbidden" and warning against "false dichotomies" like war-or-negotiation. The message also demanded attention to inflation, unemployment and price management.

threads.label: IDF strikes in Jenin and Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF said a drone strike in Jenin killed Qais Bitawi, described by Shin Bet as head of Hamas activities in the Jenin refugee camp, along with two other operatives. The military also announced the killing in Gaza's Shati camp of Ibrahim Nabil Bass, a Hamas commander who participated in the October 7 attack, and an Islamic Jihad platoon commander in Sabra.

threads.label: UK-Israel Gaza coordination friction
threads.summary: The Financial Times reported Israel is considering expelling British officials from the US-led postwar Gaza coordination centre over the E1 settlements dispute, per Times of Israel. A UK government spokesperson told the Jerusalem Post the UK remains "committed to the implementation of the 20-Point Plan in Gaza".

threads.label: Iranian domestic security and judiciary
threads.summary: IRIB reported an armed clash in Saravan in which police, IRGC and Basij forces killed one Jaysh al-Zulm member and detained six, seizing weapons; the Intelligence Ministry announced action against alleged ISIS-linked networks in Markazi. Iran International reported a 27-year-old mechanic sentenced to death for alleged Mossad cooperation, and a British-Iranian man facing 2027 UK trial over alleged Quds Force links.

events.title: Two Hamas commanders were killed in Israeli strikes in the Gaza Strip today, the military announces. One strike in Gaza City's Shati camp killed Bilal Ibrahim Saleh Raqi‘i, identified by the IDF as a commander in Hamas's anti-tank unit. A second strike in Khan Younis killed Azzam Rifaat Abd Abadala, who the military says served in Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade. The IDF justifies the strikes amid the ceasefire by saying that both terror operatives had recently advanced attacks on troops and Israeli civilians, as well as acted to restore Hamas capabilities, "while systematically violating the ceasefire." The strikes were "carried out to remove the threat," the army adds.
